Reproducibility of effects of the homeopathic dilutions 14x - 30x of gibberellic acid on growth of Lemna gibba L.
Vera Majewsky; Claudia Scherr; Sebastian Arlt; Peter Klocke; Stephan Baumgartner

Background: Reproducibility of investigations in homeopathy is still challenging. Duckweed (Lemna gibba L.), a monocotyledonous waterplant which mostly reproduces vegetatively and therefore builds genetically identical clones, may be a suitable test system for standardised trials. Aims: This study investigated if formerly observed effects of gibberellic acid 14x – 30x on growth of Lemna gibba were reproducible. Methododology: Duckweed was grown in dilutions of gibberellic acid (14x–30x) as well as once succussed (c1) and unsuccussed (c0) water control. Area-related growth rate for day 0–7 was determined by a computerised image analysis system. Three series including five independent blinded and randomised experiments each were carried out in the same way as in the original study. Only time and conductor of experiments were modified. The newly supplied primary abstract of shipped row 965 (Scherr, Simon, Spranger, & Baumgartner, 2009, Complementary Therapies in Medicine 17(2):63-70, 10.1016/j.ctim.2008.10.004) establishes a unique compound method and finding fingerprint under Codebook Step 2 (identified_by = description). Scherr et al. (2009) grew Lemna gibba L. for 7 days in decimal potencies 14x-30x versus unsuccussed and succussed water controls, measured frond area-related growth rate r(area) for day 0-7 via computerised image analysis across series of five to six independent randomized, blinded experiments per substance alongside repeated systematic negative control (SNC) water experiments, and evaluated global F-tests followed by protected Fisher's LSD tests. Among four substances screened in Scherr et al. (2009) (gibberellic acid, kinetin, argentum nitricum, Lemna minor), gibberellic acid 14x-30x yielded the most pronounced effect (p = 0.0002) and decreased r(area) day 0-7 (protected LSD p < 0.05). Majewsky et al. (2012) isolate that exact gibberellic acid 14x-30x arm and repeat three five-experiment blinded, randomized series plus three five-experiment SNC series ('carried out in the same way as in the original study. Only time and conductor of experiments were modified'), explicitly contrasting their third-series growth increase with 'decreasing in the former study.'
